review: Reviewed Wren's round-8 request (Cultivate meadow roots: a learnable, feasible way to propagate and tend edible meadow roots, with unknown inputs and costs) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 3): a general cultivation operation with modes plant, tend, inspect and end; a hand planting trial of one whole owned root in two rounds and 3 energy (1.5 per completed round) that first prepares and records the site and then transfers the root after revalidating location, occupancy and input; a 0.2-energy probe inspection; tending only when a real input and effect are implemented, otherwise refused before costs; production only from a coded establishment and growth rule, otherwise a planting and monitoring precursor. Inspecting the handlers grounded the propagule question: the existing seed dispersal in open-ecology.ts turns one actual stock unit of any living plant (growth interval > 0, fish excluded) into a seedling 'seed or vegetative propagule' with stock 0, a stock ceiling of min(4, parent capacity), the parent's growth interval and a first dispersal 600 rounds later, which establishes and grows under the same rule as natural plants. A whole harvested unit is therefore a supported propagule and production is grounded, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented cultivate-plants@1 in scope long-ex16 (learning 3; the ability serializes to 3,025 code units). Plant: inputStackId names one whole owned, untreated, unspoiled food unit (quantity 1) whose origin is a living plant of the same food; x, y name a 0.25 m plot in reach on hand-workable ground (the existing long-planting-site rule: ordinary soil, no water or wet bank, waterlogging at most 0.1, clear of people and reserved objects) with soil moisture 0.3-1.2, 0.6 m clear of objects and fewer than 3 plants of that food or prepared plots within 5 m (the dispersal law's own conditions). Every check runs before any cost, so a refusal spends nothing. Round 1 (1.5 energy) escrows the unit, still owned, carried and ageing, and creates the prepared plot (cultivation-site-prepared). Round 2 (1.5 energy) rechecks reach, site, unit and energy, moves the unit with its origin, mass and age into the plot as an unowned reserved stack that cannot be eaten or used, records its condition at transfer, and gives the plot exactly the seedling data the dispersal law gives a natural propagule (cultivation-propagule-planted; no food is created). The plot then gains establishment only from actual temperature, light, soil moisture, waterlogging and season. At the existing threshold (12, or 60 for woody plants) the unit is absorbed into the new plant: it leaves the food stocks and its mass is recorded (cultivation-plot-established). Stock then grows by one unit per growth interval up to the ceiling (cultivation-crop-matured at the first unit) and is harvested only through unchanged gather. If the buried unit spoils first under the existing ageing law, the plot dies, stops growing and is no longer a food source (cultivation-trial-failed). An unworked round, too little energy, leaving reach or a changed site pauses without charge (cultivation-work-paused). Plant resumes the person's own unfinished work and pays only the remaining round (cultivation-work-resumed). End takes one round and no energy, acts only on the person's own unfinished work, returns the unit once in its current condition and clears the empty site (cultivation-trial-ended). Death before transfer leaves the unit where the person died. A transferred unit stays planted, and nothing is refunded. Inspect (one round, 0.2 energy) runs the baseline probe observation on a plot or plant source in reach and adds an unverified personal record of visible lifecycle, stage, stock, soil and weather (cultivation-condition-observed). Verified findings come only from the probe's existing dated-change rule, which deduplicates across probe and cultivation. Tend is refused before any cost. This scope has no carried water, fertilizer or soil amendment, no input can change a plot's moisture, and crowding affects only dispersal, so no treatment input or effect exists and treatment_applied is never emitted. Also not implemented: destructive sampling of a planted specimen (the probe's material modes need an owned unreserved stack and measure load, water or heat response, not viability, and digging up a buried unit is not represented; a unit can still be probed before planting), a stressed label, and any satisfaction. The planting event carries no qualified flag, so no practice milestone, short pleasure or care satisfaction is awarded, and planting or failure gives no nutrition or comfort. Modeling assumptions: a whole harvested unit of a living plant is that plant's propagule, as in the dispersal law, for every food with a growth cycle and an ageing lifetime (so the root and berry, and also nuts, fruit, tubers and fungi). Hand preparation is limited to ordinary soil and needs no tool. The site conditions are the dispersal law's. Hand-loosened soil is not a lasting represented state, so ending or failing before transfer leaves no object. Water and nutrients are represented only by the growth rule's climate moisture, soil moisture, waterlogging and depletion terms, with no separate ledger. The plot keeps the source's growth interval and a stock ceiling of at most 4. A dead plot stays as an empty marked position. Plants that an established plot later disperses are ordinary plants. Reuse is recorded in the package: ex15 cultivation-trial@1's law constants, treated-unit list, ageing, plant, observation-input, footprint and reach helpers through new exports that leave ex15 behavior unchanged (ex7-ex15 replay compatibility identical), and its cultivation-trial drawing; also the unchanged open-ecology.ts growth law, forest-environment.ts ageing, long-planting-site.ts, collective-work.ts escrow and paid work, open-foundation.ts probe and personal records, and base gather. Tests cover learning, the paid rounds, conservation, establishment equal to a natural control seedling, absorption, stock and gather, rot failure, cost-free refusals, pause, resume and planter-only end, inspection, another food (berry), dispersed offspring and death.
